title: Tar Pit
author: MoonShaft
tags: I don’t know how to format
summary:
The dark was pressing in all around Optimus, a thick sludge that weighed on him like a rockfall, heavy and suffocating. You would assume it would be quiet here, in this strange, suspended place- but it was deafening. The soft, young voice of a boy would sometimes cut through, calling out, begging him to transform, to run, to stop whatever destruction he was causing. When this happened, it was like the sludge thinned to water, allowing him a brief glance at the world and his actions, but he just couldn’t reach the surface. His heavy metal frame made him sink lower and lower, no matter how hard he tried to swim upwards, until the voice faded and he was once again alone in darkness.
Optimus snapped his optics open, his intake quicker than normal, relaxing only when he identified the roof of his small room at his base. The dream- or memory, more like it- whilst it was most definitely not pleasant, didn't hurt as much as it once had. He had seen and felt the memory over and over, waiting in the shadows to drag him back.
 
Or: Optimus struggles to come to terms with his new Dino alt mode.

title: Sunk Cost Fallacy
author: Sunset_Mountain_Lion
tags: Inspired by an AU of an AU
Alternate Universe of an Alternate Universe of an Alternate Universe
He reads as a kid to them despite being an adult by human standards
summary:
It turns out that being wired into giant war machines doesn’t play nice with human brains. The Earth Mechanical Defense Force, or EMDF, learned that the hard way when their pilots started going… neurotic, let’s say, after a few missions.
The obvious solution to that problem was to simply wire the pilot into their mecha permanently, that way their mind wasn’t being strained by the constant in and out. Unfortunately that strategy backfired and the pilots started going neurotic much, much faster, and this time they were giant and made of metal and much harder to put down.
So, the obvious next step would be to pull the plug on that idea and go back to the drawing board, right? No, that’s ridiculous, the next step was obviously to simply…
Make the mecha forget they’d ever been human in the first place.
Somewhere along the line someone should have pulled the plug, but they’d already invested so much into the project, and you know what they say about sunk cost fallacy.

author: RevelBoo

summary: Tumblr ask that prompted the work:How’s it going, Revel? So, I was reflecting here: some bots, no matter how much they care about their respective humans, still feel a certain strangeness, modesty, or guilt about the fact that they are, well, humans—and that their relationship is interspecies. Regardless of the reason—whether it’s Fulcrum, who has a phobia of organics, Tarn, who sees humans as worms, or ES Soundwave, who hates our species—would any of them strongly wish their partner were Cybertronian? Would they dream about it, something like, “It would be so much easier if you were like that”? And most importantly, would they verbalize it to their human? I imagine that some (like the ones mentioned earlier: Tarn and ES Soundwave) at a certain point in the relationship’s development wouldn’t really care if it hurt the human. Others, like Shockwave, I imagine wouldn’t even realize that it could hurt their partner’s feelings. Because, even though they might think, “Wow, would they want me to be human too and have a normal relationship,” I think with humans it would basically be the same, and then your partner comes along and says to your face “I wish you were different”

Hell hath no fury like a dragon queen whose hoard is threatened.
In the smoldering aftermath of Mission City, Smaug thought the war was over. She was wrong. Megatron rises from the dead with an obsession reforged in the abyss, and this time his "darling" won't slip from his claws so easily. An ancient evil—the Fallen, a Prime who turned his back on creation—stirs beneath the sands of Egypt, and the fire in Smaug's chest responds to his call like a tuning fork against a dying star. He wants her flame to ignite a machine that will devour the sun.
But the Decepticons aren't the only danger circling her hoard. Optimus Prime's restraint is fracturing under a devotion he can no longer disguise as duty. Bumblebee's adoration is deepening into something fierce and territorial. And Megatron—resurrected and starving for the one treasure he could never conquer—will raze the galaxy to hear her say his name.
When the Fallen's plan threatens to extinguish the sun itself, Smaug will face the one thing more dangerous than an army of Decepticons: the terrifying possibility that she might actually need someone other than herself.
The saying has it wrong. Hell hath no fury like a woman scorned?
Try a dragon.

author: Aurisal

tags: The outline is beautiful but reality is harsh.
summary:
TFP×IDW[A smuggling case temporarily saved Megatron, who unexpectedly arrived in the IDW world. What terrible fact did he discover? How is the chain of benefits conveyed behind it formed?]
A Space Bridge accident hurls Megatron out of a universe where the war has never ended, flinging him into another Cybertron—one still struggling to its feet after the wreckage of its own. There he comes face to face with a version of himself who has already set the fusion cannon aside, pinning an Autobot insignia where the Decepticon brand used to be. They are two identical mechs, and yet they stand at the opposite ends of a four-million-year fork in the road, forced at last to ask the same question: What did we start fighting for in the first place?
This is not a story that sets out to decide who was right. Nor is it a story about who was wrong. What it traces, rather, is how belief—once sharp enough to cut a new world into being—gets worn down in the grinding machinery of war. Twisted. Buried under tactics and casualties and the weight of choices that can never be unmade. But here is the thing about belief: it has a way of enduring. Forgotten, maybe. Never truly dead.

title: Predacon Inheritance
author: OtomeGirl4Ever
tags: “It Shouldn’t Fit But It Does” (My Beta Made Me Put This)
summary:
Shockwave succeeded where nature had failed. With Megatron’s permission, he rewrote Starscream’s frame into a Carrier-type, turning the Seeker into the perfect vessel for his next experiment: proving that Seeker and Predacon CNA could produce hybrid eggs strong enough to swell the Decepticon warlord’s army.
But Shockwave made one fatal error.
He studied Starscream’s chassis. He studied Predaking’s genetic code. He studied fertility, compatibility, and war-born evolution. What he did not study was Starscream’s mutant spark.
Now, with Predaking’s CNA spreading deeper through him, Starscream’s body begins to change in ways no one predicted. Not just carrier. Not just Seeker. Something older. Something hungrier. Something Predacon.
And by the time Shockwave understands what he has awakened, Starscream may no longer be anyone’s experiment.

title: You Can’t Fight Fate
author: cman710
tags: Prowl Bluestreak and Smokescreen Live Together
summary:
Logical, serious Prowl feels he’s met his match when the Autobot’s latest philanthropic venture pairs him with fifteen year old Jeffrey Devlin.
Jeff is a snarky ball of energy fresh out of juvie. He isn’t looking for a parent, a mentor, or even friends - let alone any kind of community service.
It’s a pair that couldn’t, and shouldn’t work.

summary:
The pain.
The burning sensation emitted from his open wounds - blackened like charcoal, open wires of nerve trembling at the open air flowing through his body as energon speckles out of his wound to the open abyss beneath him.
Then came the numbness. 
The slow fading of his consciousness - his last gaze set on the bot he trusted - loved the most. He wants to reach out - to push him away from the path he’s about to pass through - the path of violence and vengeance. And yet, all he could do was mutter nothingness.
“D… No…” His last words - so small, so insignificant. A far cry from his old self - his old life. A life he had sacrificed for a dream - a hope for a better future for every one of his peers and friends. How fate rarely plays in one’s interest.

Swindle’s mouth twisted into that confused, nervous line, optics flitting between them and most concerningly the unfamiliar Seeker. Blast Off’s wings jittered once before lowering. Vortex’s rotors spun once, visor flaring as they stiffened, glare nearly turning to Starscream before Brawl leaned in, awaiting Onslaught’s orders.
Well, he couldn’t leave his team hanging. Not again.
“We’ll obey,” Onslaught said, meeting Starscream’s optics, bright red. “For now.”
Starscream’s optics gleamed.
“Excellent.”

summary:
Months have passed since the gods were defeated, the Solver and the Chaos Bringer having both been banished back into the shadows were they belonged. Peace finally returned upon Copper-9’s icy surface, yet tranquility hadn’t. Following Megatron’s departure, the decay of the world where Uzi and her friends lived was starting to become impossible to ignore. Resources were becoming scarce, plans for the future felt distant, and the hope that’d been rekindled following their last victory was starting to dwindle.
It was in the middle of these dark times that Soundwave, Megatron’s most loyal soldier, miraculously escaped the Shadowzone, finding his way upon the cold exoplanet. Fully unaware that the Decepticons have been disbanded, his loyalty to the cause he had served all his life remains unflinching. Even on this strange world of little machines, he thinks only of conquest in his master’s name, ready to seize this planet by himself as it lays in stagnation. He is a Decepticon, and he shall see to it that this world knows the glory he had sought to bring Cybertron.
No matter the cost.

They land on Jazz.

Starscream’s stare is… Different.
Calculating. Predatory. Uncomfortably sharp, like a dagger pressed under his chin.
“You.” Starscream says, pointing with the mug. “New.”
Jazz snaps a salute a half-klik faster than regulation.
“Yes, sir. Adagio, sir.”
“I didn’t ask.” Starscream sneers.

title: The Heir Protocol

Not officially. But the longer the Autobots watch, the more the room stops looking like a commander’s berth and begins looking like a cage with familiar walls. Starscream is being monitored. Measured. Fed altered energon. Studied in silence.Then Megatron enters with Shockwave, and the truth becomes colder than torture.The energon was never meant only to weaken him. It was meant to change him. To prepare him. To make the tricolor seeker fertile enough to carry Megatron’s heirs naturally. Shockwave speaks of progress like Starscream is an experiment. Megatron speaks of him like he is already owned.And when Megatron mentions how the Minicons follow Starscream, trust him, and seek his care, the Autobots understand the full horror.Megatron does not see kindness.He sees proof that Starscream will make the perfect carrier for his heirs.

"Hold on, now," Wheeljack interjected, squinting suspiciously at the Minicon who stiffly sat upon Ultra Magnus' lifeless corpse like a trophy - or like a ride. And it was easy at first, that's the thing. Deceptively easy, even, to sit here with his datapad while Drift would lazily thrust in and out of his aft for a few kliks at a time. The reality of this arrangement, however, had only hit Perceptor squarely when there had been multiple warnings about voiding his tanks popping up in his HUD. That makes it painfully real, and faced with the act of having to relieve himself like this fills him with terrible anxiety edged with a sick sense of arousal, made only worse by every throb that Drift's spike gives inside of him.
Drift speaks, then. "You need to void your tanks yet?"
It’s hard to push the words out, even. Shame is usually something he doles out when it comes to Drift, never something that he spares for himself, exactly. To be on the receiving end of this an intense, unfamiliar thrill. Perceptor bows his helm, ashamed to murmur out a yes in response.
A glutton for punishment; if only Perceptor didn't find so much pleasure in his indignification.

Gathering his courage, he spoke in a soft voice. He conjured as much strength as he could muster, since he was honestly scared shitless. “My… my name is Cade Yeager.” He cringed at his stuttering, so much for showing no fear.
Before he could say more, he was staring down the barrel of the titan’s gun. “Please,” he quickly said, putting his hands up in a show of being defenseless – he just prayed that gesture was universal enough. “You look injured. Let me help you. I know my way around metal, so I’m sure I can help.” He pleaded, not just for his life but strangely out of sincerity too.
The giant must have sensed his genuine effort through his terror, and after a few tense seconds, the barrel of the gun began to lower, staggering until it fell away completely. The gun shifted back into a hand, and the metal creature made another deep cough.
Or

Megatron and Optimus Prime had finally forged a Peace Treaty they and all of their people could abide by as they rebuilt their cities and planet now that the All-spark had been returned to the well and the matrix of leadership was fully restored. There had still been a lot of infighting, but finally, when it seemed like everyone finally got along, the news of their millions of years long war had ended and it reached the Quintessons. They believed they had a claim over the Cybertronian people and knew no one else in the galaxy would even try to stop them.
They didn't know what had struck them when it finally occurred. They fought. But the Quintessons weren't here to kill. They were here to conquer and control once more. The tide of this new war was in the people's favour until the impossible occurred, and both leaders were taken alongside many more of the people's brethren in one swoop of destruction and deceit.
Now, inside the Quintesson spire, a cage barely large enough for the two war mechs. The two unarmed leaders struggle to find comfort or escape.

title: The Cyborg Series, Book Four: "Out of the Past, and into the Darkness"
author: BetaTheCyberNinja
tags: They are finally getting together omg
summary:
Summer has come and gone, as has fall and the brutal Dakota winters. An entire year since Shockwave’s arrival to earth and our teams’ separation. It hasn’t been a quiet year. Far from it. Shockwave has hit the ground running with his predacon cloning production. And every time we lock horns, another predacon is at Megatron’s beck and call. Also, how the fuck is Shockwave planning on Cyberforming earth?Just add it to the list of world-ending things we need to stop, I guess.Despite the constant battles, something has . . . changed. With me. Going through the usual motions has stayed the same, but it all just seems . . . easier. The days go by quicker. I smile more.
I know, I’m just as stunned myself.
I thought I had confronted all of the past I needed to when we were on Cybertron. But, there’s some old ties here on Earth that are rearing their heads – but unlike the horrors of Shockwave’s laboratory and the DJD’s torture methods, they are the source of some pretty good memories.Just hope it doesn’t put the Colonel over the edge, I piss him off enough as it is.My designation is Beta-04, and this is the fourth part of my story.

title: Transformers: Ironclad Rising
author: Colossus_Prime
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary:
They were built to be perfect. They became something else. Ironclad was created as part of a secret Decepticon experiment - six brothers designed to merge into a single unstoppable weapon. But something went wrong. Something changed.
Instead of loyalty... they chose freedom. Now alone on a war-torn Cybertron, Ironclad survives the only way he knows how: by tearing his enemies apart and rebuilding himself from what remains. Each scar tells a story. Each stolen insignia marks another life taken. And through it all... he sings.
Soft lullabies echo through scrapyards and battlefields alike-calm, almost comforting... until you realize they're meant for you. Caught between the Autobots who don't fully trust him and the Decepticons who fear him, Ironclad walks a razor-thin line between hero and horror.
Because sometimes...The only way to survive war is to become something worse than it.
DISCLAIMER: I don't own Transformers. Rights to the franchise go to Hasbro, Takara Tomy, and Paramount.

title: This Place is Made for Fools (and I'm Seeking Solace)
author: mrcandle
tags: The Transformers: More Than Meets the Eye (IDW)
summary:
“You’re not being pitied,” he said again, more firmly now. “You’re a good person, Megs.”
Megatron circled Rodimus’s wrist, his optics glinting in the club’s harsh light. “You’re a fool if you believe that,” he muttered, running his thumb over Rodimus’s palm.
Rodimus snorted. “You’re stupid if you don’t. You’re good to me.”
OR;
The one thing Rodimus wants more than anything else is to make his crew happy aboard the Lost Light. Actually, that's the second thing he wants. The first is his co-captain—professionally, of course. Megatron isn't much better. His spark tells him to make Rodimus the happiest mech who's ever lived and his frame says to just be satisfied with what he's got. His processor says to bash his helm in until he doesn't think about it anymore.
Both make it everybody else's problem.

summary:
"This a bad time to say I got the touch?""Better yet, I think ya have the power. Or however that lyric goes."
IN WHICH a girl hums through life in quiet rhythms, but for every thousand lives she's lived, each time, the tempo stumbles. Each time, something intervenes. Each time, she forgets who the song was meant for.
Until the sky splits open, and a new melody crashes into her world. They call themselves Cybertronians. With them comes a rhythm that begins to thread through the silence, carried by a name that pulses like a beat beneath her skin.
They bring chaos, sure, but also family. And for a moment, everything feels in tune.
Without fail, she falls again and again, across realities rewritten, trapped in the same fractured harmony.
But the AllSpark hums louder now. She can hear its presence.
Because they were never supposed to be there.But maybe... they were exactly what was needed.
Because sometimes, the song isn't about being heard.Sometimes, it's about who listens.

title: Devastator: Origin of the Constructicons
author: Valclaron
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary:
Cybertron was built by hands the Senate never bothered to see.
Scrapper, Hook, Bonecrusher, Long Haul, Mixmaster, and Scavenger were laborers long before they became soldiers. They carried the weight of a world that dismissed them, repaired what others abandoned, and survived beneath a caste system that had no place for their worth.
Then Megatron’s revolution begins to move through the cracks.
Drawn into a war that reshapes their purpose, the six builders find themselves under Megatron’s command and Shockwave’s scrutiny. What begins as labor, loyalty, and necessity becomes an experiment unlike anything Cybertron has ever seen.
One mind.
One body.
Six lives forced to become something more.
Devastator.
As the war escalates and the Senate’s power begins to fracture, the Constructicons must learn to survive not only their enemies, but the strain of becoming a weapon large enough to change Cybertron forever.
The Senate will fall.
Devastator will rise.
And Cybertron will never be the same.

“Their intakes?” D-16 was confused. “Were they fueling?” He'd thought the only thing you could do with intakes was consume energon and speak with a vocalizer. He guessed they were used for expressions, too, but D-16 failed to understand what else an intake could be used for.
“That's what I thought! But they didn't have any energon with them.” Orion thought for a moment. “It was more like… smashing their derma together.”
“What.”

summary:
When Optimus Prime finds Starscream hidden away during a brief and dangerous seeker heat, one mistake changes the course of the war.
Cycles later, Starscream discovers he is carrying Optimus Prime’s sparkling. Desperate, frightened, and with nowhere else to go, he turns to the Autobot leader for help — only to be met with cold reality. Optimus has Elita-One, a future already imagined, and a war to win. There is no place in that future for Starscream or the sparkling he carries.
Unable to end the life growing inside him, Starscream does the unthinkable: he tells Megatron the truth.
At first, Megatron sees only a weapon. Optimus Prime’s heir could be shaped, trained, and turned against him. But plans made in cruelty do not always survive the fragile weight of a sparkling in his arms.
And when the child’s first word is “Sire,” Megatron realizes he may have already lost the war he started inside his own spark.

When his optics first come online, B-127 first sees the sky. The Well surges with power only feet from him, giving him a fond farewell even as his memory of crawling from it fades only moments after. His protoform is new and small, his body whirs with clicks and hissing as parts fall into place and his spark begins to glow all on its own, no longer sustained by Primus’ crafting hand.
It will grow, with time, his plating still a shining, unburdened silver. Glistening with its lack of abrasions and experience. Efficiency programs slot into place, and his processor works to teach him what little it already knows. His T-cog spins in his side, inactive now as New Sparks usually are, but it will burst with Energon and life soon enough.
